questions.prompt: Why does protection against regressions matter more as a software system grows?

options.text: Larger systems have fewer bugs, so they need tests only when someone introduces a regression intentionally.
Growing codebases gain hidden coupling and unpredictable interactions, so small changes can break existing behavior.
Regression tests remove the need to refactor, so teams can focus only on new features.
Regressions occur only in legacy systems because modern applications resist them.

questions.prompt: What does protection against regressions measure for an automated test?

options.text: How quickly the test runs compared with other test types.
How well the test catches previously working behavior that breaks after a code change.
How easy the test suite is to maintain over time.
How many features developers can add before updating the test.
